A.actClause: AN ACT to amend the personal property law, in relation to providing consumers with greater protection in rental purchase agreements; and to repeal certain provisions of such law relating thereto
A.memo:
BILL NUMBER:A3083A

TITLE  OF BILL:   An act to amend the personal property law, in relation
to providing consumers with greater protection in rental purchase agree-
ments; and to repeal certain provisions of such law relating thereto

Purpose Or General Idea Of Bill:    The  purpose  of  this  bill  is  to
increase consumer protections in the rent-to-own industry and to provide
rent-to-own merchants with increased regulatory guidance.

Summary Of Specific Provisions:  This bill would make significant chang-
es  to  the Rent to Own Program Law (Article 11 of the Personal Property
Law), most notably  by  establishing  well-defined  price  controls  and
requiring  rent-to-own  merchants  to  provide  consumers  with enhanced
disclosures.

Under current law, the total amount a rent-to-own customer must  pay  in
order  to  acquire  ownership of the merchandise is limited to twice the
"cash price" of the merchandise, which is defined as the price at  which
the  merchant  would sell the merchandise to the consumer for cash. This
bill would implement a significantly more robust  price  control  scheme
by:

o  establishing a formula for determining the maximum cash price for new
and used goods based on the merchant's  actual  cost  of  acquiring  the
merchandise;

o  establishing  a formula for determining the maximum amount a consumer
must pay in order acquire ownership of the merchandise; and

o providing consumers the right to acquire ownership of the  merchandise
within  three  months  of  signing an agreement by paying the cash price
minus all payments paid.

The bill would require rent-to-own merchants to provide  consumers  with
enhanced  disclosures.  Specifically, the bill would require rent-to-own
merchants to:

o include a "disclosure box" containing the total  amount  of  payments,
cost  of  rental, cash price, amount of each payment, number of payments
and the rental period, along with a layman's explanation  of  the  first
three  terms  on  every  rental-purchase  agreement. This disclosure box
would also be required to be affixed to all merchandise;

o include a notice containing a layman's explanation of the  rental-pur-
chase transaction in each rental agreement;

o  provide  notice  to consumers of the early purchase option, including
the total amount necessary to acquire  ownership,  on  three  occasions;
thirty to sixty days before the ninety days same as cash option expires,
the  date  the  consumer  has  made one-half of all payments required to

obtain ownership, and the date a consumer requests information regarding
the amount required to purchase the merchandise; and

o provide customers with a copy of the signed rental-purchase agreement.

In addition, the bill would:

o provide consumers with the right to reinstate a rental-purchase agree-
ment  within  one  year  of  the  return  of the merchandise and require
merchants to provide notice of the consumer's  right  to  reinstate  the
agreement upon repossession of merchandise;

o exempt Sundays and federally recognized holidays from the time periods
used to determine late charges or reinstatement fees; and

o require merchants to maintain rental merchandise in good working order
while the agreement is in effect free of charge.

Justification:   New York's "Rent to Own Program Law" (Article 11 of the
Personal Property Law) was enacted in 1986  and  has  not  been  updated
since  that  time.  The law caps the total amount a consumer must pay in
order to acquire ownership of the merchandise at twice the "cash  price"
of  the merchandise, which is defined as the price at which the merchant
would sell the merchandise to the consumer for cash. According to  memo-
randa  issued  at  the  time  of  the  law's enactment, several consumer
groups, as well as Attorney General Robert Abrams, voiced  concern  that
rent-to-own  merchants  could  abuse their authority to set cash prices.
According to reports and testimony received at  recent  Assembly  public
hearings,  rent-to-own merchants often sidestep the intent of the law by
setting cash prices as high as  twice  the  price  found  for  the  same
merchandise at nearby retail outlets.

This  bill would establish a formula for rent-to-own merchants to use in
determining cash prices. This would ensure  that  rent-to-own  customers
pay   fair   prices  and  provide  much-needed  regulatory  guidance  to
merchants, by removing any uncertainty concerning the  setting  of  cash
prices.  This  bill  would also significantly strengthen existing law by
implementing several new and enhanced consumer disclosures.   For  exam-
ple, rent-to-own merchants would be required to include a disclosure box
containing  important  information for consumers, similar to the Schumer
Box currently required to be included in credit card solicitations.

This legislation recognizes that rent-to-own merchants provide a  unique
transaction  utilized  by  many  consumers.  This bill would ensure that
consumers are aware of their rights and obligations before entering into
a rent-to-own agreement and establish reasonable price  controls,  while
allowing  the rent-to-own industry to continue to offer its unique prod-
uct in New York state.

Prior Legislative History:  2007-2008: A.66-C - Advanced to Third  Read-
ing
2005-2006: A.230 - Referred to Consumer Affairs and Protection

2003-2004: A.3511 - Referred to Consumer Affairs and Protection
2001-2002: A.4018 - Referred to Consumer Affairs and Protection
Fiscal Implications For State And Local Governments:  None to the State.
Effective Date:  This act shall take effect on the one hundred eightieth
day  after  it shall have become a law and shall apply to all agreements
entered into or offered on or after such date.

C.memo:
BILL NUMBER:A3083C

TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the personal property law, in relation
to providing consumers with greater protection in rental purchase agree-
ments; and to repeal certain provisions of such law relating thereto

Purpose Or General Idea Of Bill:  The purpose of this bill is to
increase consumer protections in the rent-to-own industry and to provide
rent-to-own merchants with increased regulatory guidance.

Summary Of Specific Provisions:  This bill would make significant chang-
es to the Rent to Own Program Law (Article 11 of the Personal Property
Law) by providing for enhanced disclosures and providing for a compre-
hensive study of rent-to-own pricing, the rent-to-own business model,
and fair and reasonable price controls to be performed by the Attorney
General, in conjunction with the Consumer Protection Board and the
Department of Economic Development that would serve as the basis for
improving the law's price control provisions.

The bill would require rent-to-own merchants to provide consumers with
enhanced disclosures. Specifically, the bill would require rent-to-own
merchants to:

o include a "disclosure box" containing the total amount of payments,
cost of rental, cash price, amount of each payment, number of payments
and the rental period, along with a layman's explanation of the first
three terms on every rental-purchase agreement. This disclosure box
would also be required to be affixed to all merchandise;

o include a notice containing a layman's explanation of the rental-pur-
chase transaction in each rental agreement;

o provide notice to consumers of the early purchase option, including
the total amount necessary to acquire ownership, on three occasions;
thirty to sixty days before the early purchase option expires, the date
the consumer has made one-half of all payments required to obtain owner-
ship, and the date a consumer requests information regarding the amount
required to purchase the merchandise; and

o provide customers with a copy of the signed rental-purchase agreement.

This bill would also require the Attorney General, in conjunction with
the Consumer Protection Board and the Department of Economic Develop-
ment, in consultation with representatives from the rent-to-own indus-
try, the business community, and consumer advocates, to perform a review
of rent-to-own pricing, and if the Attorney General determines that it
is necessary for such review, a survey of retailers located within the
state to determine the average markup applied by retailers to consumer
goods offered for sale to the public. The Attorney General, Consumer
Protection Board, and the Department of Economic Development would also
report to the Governor and Legislature on their findings and make joint
recommendations as to appropriate and fair formulas for determining cash

prices and the maximum cost of rental for rent-to-own merchandise to the
Governor and Legislature. This report would provide the Legislature with
the information necessary to determine a fair formula for rent-to-own
merchants to use in setting cash prices. The Board and the Department
would also be required to.

In addition, the bill would:

o provide consumers the right to acquire ownership of the merchandise
within three months of signing an agreement by paying the cash price
minus all payments paid;

o exempt Sundays and federally recognized holidays from the time periods
used to determine late charges or reinstatement fees;

o require rent-to-own merchants to offer customers extended rein-
statement rights; and

o require merchants to provide notice of the consumer's right to rein-
state the agreement upon repossession of merchandise.

Justification:  New York's "Rent to Own Program Law" (Article 11 of the
Personal Property Law) was enacted in 1986 and has not been updated
since that time. The law caps the total amount a consumer must pay in
order to acquire ownership of the merchandise at twice the "cash price"
of the merchandise, which is defined as the price at which the merchant
would sell the merchandise to the consumer for cash. According to memo-
randa issued at the time of the law's enactment, several consumer
groups, as well as Attorney General Robert Abrams, voiced concern that
rent-to-own merchants could abuse their authority to set cash prices.
According to recent reports and testimony received at the September 20,
2006 and October 5, 2006 Assembly public hearings on financial services
for low-income consumers, rent-to-own merchants often sidestep the
intent of the law by setting cash prices as high as twice the price
found for the same merchandise at nearby retail outlets.

This bill would provide for a study to be performed by the Attorney
General, in conjunction with the Consumer Protection Board and Depart-
ment of Economic Development on rent-to-own pricing which would serve as
the basis for establishing fair and reasonable formulas for rent-to-own
merchants to use in determining cash prices. This would ensure that
rent-to-own customers pay fair prices and provide much-needed regulatory
guidance to merchants, by removing any uncertainty concerning the
setting of cash prices. This bill would also significantly strengthen
existing law by implementing several new and enhanced consumer disclo-
sures. For example, rent-to-own merchants would be required to include a
disclosure box containing important information for consumers, similar
to the Schumer Box currently required to be included in credit card
solicitations.

This legislation recognizes that rent-to-own merchants provide a unique
transaction utilized by many consumers. This bill would ensure that

consumers are aware of their rights and obligations prior to entering
into a rent-to-own agreement. The bill would also provide the Legisla-
ture with the information and recommendations necessary to establish
reasonable price controls. This pragmatic approach to price controls
will ensure that consumers pay reasonable prices, while allowing the
rent-to-own industry to continue to offer its unique product in New York
state.

ing
2005-2006: A.230 - Referred to Consumer Affairs and Protection
2003-2004: A.3511 - Referred to Consumer Affairs and Protection
2001-2002: A4018 - Referred to Consumer Affairs and Protection

Fiscal Implications For State And Local Governments:  None to the State.

Effective Date:  This act shall take effect on the one hundred eightieth
day after it shall have become a law and shall apply to all agreements
entered into or offered on or after such date.

summary: Provides for greater protections to consumers in rental purchase agreements; defines certain terms; provides greater disclosure to consumer regarding the amount, number and times at which various payments relating to such an agreement are due and owing; makes various provisions regarding the method and information required to be disclosed in advertising for such agreements; provides for a right of reinstatement upon repossession.
